children.prose: `normalize(value)` clamps a number to the inclusive range 0–100: negatives become 0, values above 100 become 100, and in-range values pass through unchanged.
qualifications: Source-level behavior only; JavaScript edge cases such as NaN are not specially handled.

children.prose: `nextSequence()` owns a module-scoped counter initialized to 0. Each call increments it before returning, so successive calls yield 1, 2, 3, and so on for that module instance; it accepts no caller input and exposes no reset.
qualifications: Sequence lifetime and sharing depend on runtime module instantiation; no runtime execution was observed.
Unbounded JavaScript-number growth can eventually lose integer precision; the source has no overflow handling.

inconsistencies.reason: The README says all entry exports are pure/stateless and return the same result for the same arguments. The re-exported `nextSequence` instead mutates module-scoped `sequence`, so repeated zero-argument calls return different values.
qualifications: The README is nearby repository documentation; its applicability was not mechanically established, but it explicitly names this entry and both exports.
